meaning: A policy built from a model that reads images and text, with the robot's joint readings added as an input and an action chunk as the output.
A network pretrained on images and text from the web that takes pictures and a prompt and writes text.
The vision-language model inside a VLA, which turns the camera images and the instruction into tokens and understands the scene and the request.
The smaller network attached to the backbone that reads its tokens and the robot state and outputs an action chunk; also called the action expert.
Physical Intelligence's name for the action head.
The sentence that tells a VLA which task to do, fed to the model on every call.
The image tokens and text tokens of one call, which the backbone reads once and caches for the action head.
Filling the unused slots of a fixed-width state or action vector with zeros so one model can serve robots with different numbers of joints.
A robot body: its joints, sensors and action space.
A way to generate an action chunk by starting from random noise and refining it in a few steps; section 4 covers it.
One refinement pass of the action head on its way from noise to an action chunk.
A transformer used as the network that refines noise into an output, here an action chunk.
The slow part of a robot model that reads the scene and the instruction, usually the vision-language model.
The fast part of a robot model that turns the slow part's output and the robot state into actions, usually the action head.
Times per second.
A model that predicts future video and the action chunk together, so it forecasts what the camera will see as well as what the robot should do.
A fine-tune that trains small added matrices and leaves the base weights frozen.
A small policy trained from scratch on demonstrations of one task; section 4 covers it.
A test where the object starts in positions the demonstrations covered.
A test where the object starts somewhere the demonstrations did not cover.
Video shot from the point of view of the person doing the task.
A suite of simulated manipulation tasks used as a benchmark for robot policies.
NVIDIA's compiler that turns a trained network into an optimised inference engine.
Physical Intelligence's open repository, which holds pi0, pi0-FAST and pi0.5.
Hugging Face's open robotics library, which trains and runs policies on arms such as the SO-101.
One model family in LeRobot, selected on the command line with --policy.type.
NVIDIA's onboard computer for robots, the newest of the Jetson line named in this section.
